pages.textMedium:
It was winter. Snow lay on the forest like a thick white blanket, and the pond was frozen as hard as a table.

Teddy the bear stood on the ice and looked down. Right under his feet, the fish swam round and round. They looked very relaxed. Too relaxed.
pages.textLong:
It was winter. Snow lay on the forest like a thick white blanket, and the pond was frozen as hard as a table.

Teddy the bear stood on the ice and looked down. Right under his feet, the fish swam round and round. They looked very relaxed. Too relaxed.

Teddy knocked on the ice. Knock, knock.

A fat fish swam up and looked at him through the ice. It did not hurry. It yawned, right in his face. Then it rolled over and swam away on its back.

On its BACK.

Well. Nobody yawns at a bear.
pages.scene: Teddy on all fours on the frozen pond, nose pressed to the ice, frowning down. Right under his nose, seen through the pale ice, a fat fish floats on its back with its mouth wide open in a yawn. Snowy pines behind. Lively detail: another fish is fast asleep in the water weed as if it were a hammock.

pages.textMedium:
"Fish for dinner," said Teddy. He scratched and scraped with his claws until there was a round hole in the ice.

Now all he needed was his fishing rod. Small problem. Teddy did not own a fishing rod.
pages.textLong:
"Fish for dinner," said Teddy. He scratched and scraped with his claws until there was a round hole in the ice.

Now all he needed was his fishing rod. Small problem. Teddy did not own a fishing rod.

pages.textMedium:
No rod? No problem. Teddy took a big breath and stuck his whole head down the hole.

It was so cold his ears squeaked. The fish swam up and stared at him. He snapped at one and got a mouthful of pond.

Then his head got stuck. He pulled. He wriggled. POP! Out he came, with a moustache made of ice.
pages.textLong:
No rod? No problem. Teddy took a big breath and stuck his whole head down the hole.

It was so cold his ears squeaked. The fish swam up and stared at him. He snapped at one and got a mouthful of pond.

Then his head got stuck. He pulled. He wriggled. POP! Out he came, with a moustache made of ice.
pages.scene: Side view cut through the ice: above, Teddy's big bottom and short tail stick up in the air, back paws scrabbling on the ice; below, his head is underwater in the hole, cheeks puffed, eye to eye with three unimpressed fish. Lively detail: the little orange snail on the pond floor has stopped to watch, and bubbles rise from Teddy's nose.

pages.textLong:
"What you need," said a squirrel on a snowy branch, "is a rod."

"I KNOW," said Teddy.

He broke off a long icicle. It snapped. He pulled at a pine branch. All the snow on the tree came down on his head. WHUMP.

The squirrel said nothing. It was a very loud nothing.
pages.scene: Teddy buried up to his neck in a heap of snow under a pine tree at the edge of the pond, only his cross face (with an ice moustache) and one paw holding half a broken icicle sticking out. Above him the squirrel sits on a branch that is now bare of snow, looking down with its paws on its hips. Lively detail: the other half of the icicle is stuck upright in the snow like a candle.

pages.textMedium:
But Teddy had an idea. A genius idea. He found a piece of rope. He tied one end to his short, stumpy tail. He dropped the other end down the hole.

Then he sat down, right on top of it. "Genius," said Teddy.
pages.textLong:
But Teddy had an idea. A genius idea. He found a piece of rope. He tied one end to his short, stumpy tail. He dropped the other end down the hole.

Then he sat down, right on top of it. "Genius," said Teddy.

pages.textMedium:
"That," said a squirrel on a snowy branch, "is the worst idea I have ever seen. And I once saw a moose try to climb a tree."

"Wait and see," said Teddy.

Under the ice, the fish looked at the rope. One sniffed it. One poked it. Then they went back to swimming round and round. Very relaxed.
pages.textLong:
"That," said the squirrel, "is the worst idea I have ever seen. And I once saw a moose try to climb a tree."

"Wait and see," said Teddy.

Under the ice, the fish looked at the rope. One sniffed it. One poked it. Then they went back to swimming round and round. Very relaxed.
pages.scene: The squirrel hangs upside down from a branch, nose to nose with Teddy, pointing at the rope tied to his tail. Teddy sits on the hole with his arms folded and his nose in the air, not listening. Under the ice one fish pokes the rope end with its nose while the others swim past, bored. Lively detail: the squirrel is holding a pine cone it has completely forgotten to eat.

pages.textLong:
Then — TUG. Something pulled the rope!

"A BITE!" roared Teddy. He jumped up and hauled on the rope, paw over paw, as fast as he could.

On the end of it sat a snail. A small orange snail. It looked very pleased with the ride.

Teddy put it back. "Not a word," he told the squirrel.
pages.scene: Teddy standing beside the hole, holding the dripping end of the rope up to his face. On it sits the small orange snail from the pond floor, smiling. Teddy's face is flat with disappointment. The squirrel on its branch has both paws clamped over its mouth to keep from laughing. Lively detail: two fish heads poke out of the hole, giggling bubbles.

pages.textMedium:
He waited. And he waited. His bottom got cold. His nose got cold. A snowflake landed on his ear. No fish.

To pass the time, he ate a few blueberries from his bag. Then a few more. Then all of them.

(This was not a genius idea.)
pages.textLong:
He sat back down and he waited. And he waited. His bottom got cold. His nose got cold. A snowflake landed on his ear. No fish.

To pass the time, he ate a few blueberries from his bag. Then a few more. Then all of them.

(This was not a genius idea.)

pages.textMedium:
Under the ice, the fish had found a new game. They swung on the rope. They skipped with it. One of them tied a knot in it.

Tug, tug, tug.

"A BITE!" shouted Teddy, and tried to jump up.

He could not. His bottom had frozen to the ice.

"Genius," said the squirrel.
pages.textLong:
Under the ice, the fish had found a new game. They swung on the rope. They skipped with it. One of them tied a knot in it.

Tug, tug, tug.

"A BITE!" shouted Teddy, and tried to jump up.

He could not. His bottom had frozen to the ice.

"Genius," said the squirrel.
pages.scene: Side view cut through the ice: above, Teddy pushes down on the ice with both paws, straining to stand, eyes popping, mouth stained blue, but his bottom is stuck fast with frosty sparkles around it. Below, the fish play with the rope: two swing on it, one skips over it. The squirrel smirks from its branch. Lively detail: a fat knot tied in the middle of the rope.

pages.textMedium:
An hour went by. Then Teddy's belly said: blubb.

"Shh," said Teddy. The squirrel leaned in.

His belly said: BLUBB-BLUBB. It rumbled like thunder far away. It was full of blueberries, and the blueberries wanted OUT.
pages.textLong:
An hour went by. Then Teddy's belly said: blubb.

"Shh," said Teddy. The squirrel leaned in.

His belly said: BLUBB-BLUBB. It rumbled like thunder far away. It was full of blueberries, and the blueberries wanted OUT.

"Was that thunder?" asked the squirrel.

"Yes," said Teddy.

It was not thunder. BLUBB-BLUBB-BLUBB went his belly, so loudly that the ice hummed. Right underneath him, the fish stopped swimming round and round. They looked up.

Teddy pushed with both paws. He rocked left. He rocked right. Still stuck. What would YOU do?
pages.scene: Seen from under the ice, looking up: the fish have all stopped mid-swim and stare upward with worried eyes at the round dark shape of Teddy's bottom over the hole. The rope trembles and rings of ripples spread through the water. Above the ice, small, Teddy rocks to one side with the squirrel watching. Lively detail: the orange snail has pulled itself into its shell, only its eye-stalks peeking out.

pages.textMedium:
Teddy held on. He squeezed his eyes shut. He crossed his toes. He crossed his ears, which is not easy.

The squirrel leaned down from its branch. "Don't you dare," said the squirrel.

"I can't hold it!" squeaked Teddy.
pages.textLong:
Teddy held on. He squeezed his eyes shut. He crossed his toes. He crossed his ears, which is not easy.

The squirrel leaned down from its branch. "Don't you dare," said the squirrel.

"I can't hold it!" squeaked Teddy.

pages.textMedium:
And then...

Pft.

That was all. One tiny pft, no louder than a mouse sneezing. A little purple puff floated up past Teddy's ear and away over the trees.

"Oh," said the squirrel. "Was that it?"

Teddy opened one eye. His belly went very, very quiet.

That was not it.
pages.textLong:
And then...

Pft.

That was all. One tiny pft, no louder than a mouse sneezing. A little purple puff floated up past Teddy's ear and away over the trees.

"Oh," said the squirrel. "Was that it?"

Teddy opened one eye. His belly went very, very quiet.

That was not it.
pages.scene: Teddy still sitting on the hole, one eye open, a small hopeful smile, paws on his belly. One tiny purple-blue puff, no bigger than his ear, drifts up past his head toward the treetops. The squirrel wipes its brow with relief. Lively detail: under the ice, every fish has a fin clamped over its nose.

pages.textMedium:
PRRRRRRRT-BOOM!

It was the biggest fart the forest had ever heard. Snow fell off every tree. The squirrel fell off its branch. And the ice went CRACK — crick — crack — into a thousand pieces.
pages.textLong:
PRRRRRRRT-BOOM!

It was the biggest fart the forest had ever heard. Snow fell off every tree. The squirrel fell off its branch. And the ice went CRACK — crick — crack — into a thousand pieces.

The boom rolled across the whole forest, all the way to the mountains. Trees that had been white all winter were suddenly green.

A purple cloud drifted over the treetops. It smelled of blueberries. Mostly.

Far away, in his den, grumpy old Grandpa Bear opened one eye. "Not again," he said, and went back to sleep.
pages.scene: A wide view over the winter forest: a ring of pines shaken green and bare of snow spreads out from the pond in the distance, where a purple-blue cloud rises over the treetops. In the foreground, a cutaway of a snug den, a new place for this story: grey Grandpa Bear (the one from The Fish Tornado) in bed under a quilt, one grumpy eye open. Lively detail: his nightcap has been blown sideways off his ear.

pages.textMedium:
Up shot the fish! The blast blew them right out of the pond and high into the sky, like silver fireworks.

And down went Teddy. SPLASH! Into the freezing cold water, with the rope still tied to his tail.
pages.textLong:
Up shot the fish! The blast blew them right out of the pond and high into the sky, like silver fireworks.

And down went Teddy. SPLASH! Into the freezing cold water, with the rope still tied to his tail.

pages.textMedium:
Teddy came up with a lump of ice on his head and his teeth going like a woodpecker.

No ice. No hole. No genius idea. Any other bear would have climbed out and gone home.

Teddy looked up. High above him the fish stopped, turned, and started to come down.

"Dinner," said Teddy.

Plip. Plop. PLOP.
pages.textLong:
Teddy came up with a lump of ice on his head and his teeth going like a woodpecker.

No ice. No hole. No genius idea. Any other bear would have climbed out and gone home.

Teddy looked up. High above him the fish stopped, turned, and started to come down.

"Dinner," said Teddy.

Plip. Plop. PLOP.
pages.scene: Teddy's head and shoulders sticking out of the dark water between ice floes, teeth chattering, a lump of ice sitting on his head like a hat, looking straight up with a slow grin. High above, the fish hang at the very top of their flight, just turning to fall, and the first ones splash down around him. Lively detail: the squirrel floats by on a small ice floe, clinging on with all four paws.

pages.textMedium:
"B-b-brrr!" said Teddy.

But look! All around him, fish were floating, dizzy and very surprised. Teddy paddled round and round and scooped them up — one, two, ten, twenty — until his arms were full.

Not so relaxed now, were they?
pages.textLong:
"B-b-brrr!" said Teddy.

But look! All around him, fish were floating, dizzy and very surprised. Teddy paddled round and round and scooped them up — one, two, ten, twenty — until his arms were full.

Not so relaxed now, were they?

Getting out was harder. Teddy threw the fish onto the bank, one by one. Then he climbed out and shook himself like a dog.

Every drop froze in the air. Tinkle, tinkle. And every hair on Teddy stood straight out, stiff with ice.

"You look like a hedgehog," said the squirrel. "A big one."
pages.scene: Teddy on the snowy bank of the broken pond, just finished shaking himself: his fur stands out in icy spikes all over like a giant hedgehog, red neckerchief frozen stiff, a surprised look on his face. Frozen drops hang sparkling in the air around him. A pile of dizzy fish lies in the snow. Lively detail: the squirrel sits on top of the fish pile, pointing at him and laughing.

pages.textMedium:
Then Teddy climbed out and walked home with his arms full of fish. Crunch, crunch, crunch, through the snow.

Behind him, the rope was still tied to his tail. It had frozen as stiff as a stick, and it stuck straight out.

"Look at that," said the squirrel, riding on the end of it. "Now you have a fishing rod."
pages.textLong:
Teddy walked home with his arms full of fish. Crunch, crunch, crunch, through the snow.

Behind him, the rope was still tied to his tail. It had frozen as stiff as a stick, and it stuck straight out.

"Look at that," said the squirrel, riding on the end of it. "Now you have a fishing rod."
pages.scene: Dusk in the snowy forest. Teddy trudges home along a path of deep paw prints, arms full of fish, fur still a little spiky. The rope tied to his tail has frozen stiff and sticks straight out behind him like a rod. The squirrel rides on the end of it as if on a branch, very comfortable. Lively detail: the warm yellow window of Teddy's den glows between the trees ahead.

pages.textMedium:
That evening Teddy sat by his fire, wrapped in a blanket, with his toes in a bucket of warm water. The fish sizzled in the pan.

"Genius," said Teddy, and yawned. "But next time... fewer blueberries."

And he was asleep before the last fish was done. Because even the toughest bear in the forest has to sleep sometime.
